items.title: Police hunt driver after man killed while crossing Shah Alam road
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 31 — Police are hunting for the driver of an unidentified vehicle believed to have struck a 45-year-old pedestrian, killing him in Shah Alam this morning. Shah Alam district police chief Assistant Commissioner Sarudin Samah said the victim, who is from Bangladesh, was believed to have been crossing the road when he was hit. “The victim’s body was later taken to the Forensic Department at Shah Alam Hospital for a post-mortem examination,” he said today.

items.title: Four suspects remanded after 29‑year‑old slashed with sharp weapons in brutal Kajang roadside attack
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 31 — Police have detained four men to assist investigations into a man who was found seriously injured after being attacked with sharp weapons by the roadside near Taman West Country, Kajang early Saturday morning. Kajang district police chief ACP Naazron Abdul Yusof said a police report regarding the 29-year-old victim was lodged at 2.28am and the victim is currently receiving treatment at Kajang Hospital. “The Kajang District Police Headquarters Criminal Investigation Division launched an operation to track down the suspects and successfully detained four local male suspects aged between their 20s and 30s around Kajang yesterday and early this morning,” he said in a statement here yesterday.

items.title: John Ternus to lead Apple into the age of AI
items.summary: SAN FRANCISCO, (United States): John Ternus takes over as Apple's chief executive on Tuesday, inheriting a company that towers over the smartphone market but trails its rivals in artificial intelligence. The handover ends Tim Cook's 15-year run, replacing the operations specialist who built Apple's supply chain with the engineer who built its hardware. Ternus, 51, joined Apple's design team in 2001 and worked his way up to senior vice president of hardware engineering, reporting to Cook.

items.title: Snatch thieves fail to grab woman’s handbag, but rip RM2,000 gold bracelet from her wrist outside Cheras home
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 31 — Two men on a motorcycle targeted a 49-year-old woman outside her home in Cheras, failing to snatch her handbag before ripping a RM2,000 gold bracelet from her wrist and speeding away. Kajang district police chief Assistant Commissioner Naazron Abdul Yusof said one of the men got off the motorcycle and initially tried to seize the victim’s handbag. “A Yamaha Y15ZR motorcycle carrying two unidentified male suspects approached the victim, and one of the suspects got off and tried to pull away her handbag but failed.

items.title: King Sultan Ibrahim and Queen Raja Zarith Sofiah grace Putrajaya’s grand 69th National Day parade
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 31 — Malaysia’s King and Queen, Their Majesties Sultan Ibrahim and Raja Zarith Sofiah, graced the 69th National Day celebration at Dataran Putrajaya today. Their Majesties arrived at 8am and were received by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and his wife, Datuk Seri Dr. Wan Azizah Wan Ismail, as well as Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil, who also serves as chairman of the National Day and Malaysia Day (HKHM) 2026 Main Committee. This was followed by a fly-past of five helicopters carrying the Malaysian flag and the flags of the Malaysian Armed Forces, Army, Royal Malaysian Navy and Royal Malaysian Air Force, immediately after Their Majesties took their places at the Royal Stage.

items.title: Ong Kian Ming quits DAP, to help KJ in GE16
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Former Bangi member of parliament Dr Ong Kian Ming has announced his resignation from DAP. The former international trade and industry deputy minister said that while he would no longer be an active politician, he would continue serving the nation alongside like-minded people. Ong said he would help former health minister Khairy Jamaluddin in his 16th General Election (GE16) campaign.

items.title: Sarawak air quality worsens, 4 areas record hazardous API readings
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Air quality in Sarawak worsened today, with four locations recording hazardous readings and three others entering the "very unhealthy" category as of 8.45am on National Day. Of the 68 air quality monitoring stations nationwide, one recorded good air quality, 45 were in the moderate range and 21 recorded readings ranging from unhealthy to hazardous, while no reading was available for Temerloh in Perak. Mukah recorded a sharp increase from 185 to 267, moving from unhealthy to very unhealthy.

items.title: Family outing turns to tragedy as father and eight-year-old son drown off Pengerang
items.summary: Utusan Malaysia reported that the victims were identified as Mohammad Nizam Zainal and his son, Muhammad Zamri Mikhail. The pair were found unconscious after members of the public pulled them ashore near the campsite in Kampung Punggai before firefighters arrived. Punggai Fire and Rescue Station operations commander Aldron Dey Judih@Judeh said an emergency call was received at 7.10pm.

items.title: Serian API nears 500 as four Sarawak areas hit hazardous levels
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 31 — Air pollution in Serian reached a hazardous Air Pollutant Index (API) reading of 476 this morning, as four areas in Sarawak recorded readings above the 300 mark. All four readings fall within the hazardous category. APIMS data also showed another 14 locations across six states and territories recording unhealthy API levels above 100.

items.title: Tens of thousands gather before sunrise as favourable weather lifts National Day spirit
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 31 — Dataran Putrajaya came alive this morning as tens of thousands of visitors gathered for the 2026 National Day celebrations. To ensure public safety and smooth traffic flow amid the large crowds, police have been closely monitoring traffic along the main routes around Dataran Putrajaya since early this morning. According to the Department of Environment (DOE)’s Malaysian Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) portal, the Air Pollutant Index (API) reading at the Putrajaya station stood at 79, indicating a moderate level.

items.title: Media Prima contingent joins National Day parade in Putrajaya
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: Media Prima Bhd (MPB), Malaysia's largest integrated media group, added colour to the 2026 National Day celebrations by taking part in the parade to foster patriotism and love for the country. Taking part under the Digital Connectivity Cluster, 17 employees from various departments marched along the main route at Dataran Putrajaya here alongside participants from the country's leading media and telecommunications companies. Besides MPB, the parade group included other local broadcasters and telecommunications organisations, including the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC), Radio Television Malaysia (RTM), Astro and CelcomDigi Bhd.

items.title: National Day celebrations kick off with arrival of King and Queen [WATCH]
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: The 2026 National Day celebration procession officially began following the arrival of His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, and Her Majesty Raja Zarith Sofiah, Queen of Malaysia. Their Majesties' arrival was also greeted with a Royal Salute and the national anthem, Negaraku. Sultan Ibrahim then inspected the parade and received the Royal Salute from the Main Guard of Honour, comprising four officers and 103 personnel from the First Battalion, Royal Malay Regiment, based at Perdana Camp in Sungai Besi.

items.title: Ong Kian Ming quits DAP after 14 years, rules out GE16 run but vows to campaign for Khairy
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 31 — Former Bangi MP Ong Kian Ming has resigned from DAP after 14 years, ruling out contesting the next general election or joining another political party in the near future while reaffirming his pledge to campaign for Khairy Jamaluddin if he stands in the next general election (GE16). Ong announced his departure in a Facebook post today addressed to DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke and copied to the party’s national organising secretary Khoo Poay Tiong. Ong, who joined DAP in 2012, did not give a reason for his resignation and struck an appreciative tone as he reflected on his years with the party.

items.title: PM Anwar joins Cabinet and thousands at Dataran Putrajaya for Malaysia’s 69th National Day parade
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 31 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and members of the Cabinet today joined thousands of Malaysians in celebrating the 69th National Day at Dataran Putrajaya, here. Earlier, Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi arrived at Dataran Putrajaya at 7.45am. Also present were Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil, who is also chairman of the main committee for the 2026 National Day and Malaysia Day (HKHM) celebrations, Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail, Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin and other Cabinet ministers.

items.title: Death toll from Nepal, Tibet floods, landslides rises to 804, nearly 3,300 remain missing
items.summary: In Nepal, police authorities said they have recovered 788 bodies from floods-hit areas, whereas, 2,742 people remain missing, including hundreds of foreign nationals. Chinese authorities reported 16 deaths and 546 people missing in Tibet. Search and rescue operations are underway for 2,498 people who remain missing, including 933 workers at hydropower projects, 589 foreign nationals, 127 Nepalis travelling with foreign tourists, and residents from several affected districts, local sources reported.

items.title: Patriotism starts with the choices we make
items.summary: These choices can support local entrepreneurs, safeguard jobs and boost the domestic economy. This spirit underpins "Jom Malaysia: Jom Beli Produk Malaysia", a government-led movement aimed at encouraging Malaysians to recognise, support and take pride in home-grown products and services. Encouraging people to buy local is not a new concept.Launched in 1984, the 'Kempen Beli Barangan Malaysia' (KBBM) has long promoted homegrown goods.

items.title: Negri Sembilan sets sights on 2,405 projects by 2040
items.summary: Ismail said the target would be supported by 14 investment sector focus areas, comprising nine development parcels within the Malaysia Vision Valley (MVV) area and five flagships outside MVV. [[nid:1522437]] "This reflects the state's considerable development capacity and competitiveness to support economic growth, the expansion of industrial activities, the development of new cities and the entry of domestic and foreign investments in the future." Ismail said the growth would be driven by high-impact projects in the Seremban Economic Development Zone and Port Dickson under MVV 2.0, which are expected to serve as catalysts for industrial development, investment and land use.

items.title: Crowds gather for 69th National Day celebrations in Putrajaya
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: Families arrived at Dataran Putrajaya before dawn, staking out spots along the parade route hours before the 69th National Day celebration began. Omar Muhammad said he made the trip with more than 10 family members from Semenyih, leaving home at around 3.30am and arriving shortly after 4am. Because we're from Mersing, Johor, we have to support Johor," he said.

items.title: Dear Malaysia
items.summary: SELAMAT Hari Kebangsaan and Selamat Hari Malaysia, my dear fellow Malaysians. Each year, I reflected on the many challenges facing our beloved nation; our economy, education, corruption, political reforms, climate change, artificial intelligence and the rapidly changing world around us. Many of us become husbands and wives.

items.title: Fine weather greets 69th National Day celebrations in Putrajaya
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: Fine weather accompanied the 2026 National Day celebrations at Dataran Putrajaya this morning. Based on the Malaysian Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) portal, the Air Pollutant Index (API) reading in Putrajaya stood at 79 as of 7am. The reading was categorised as moderate, but air quality remained under control and did not affect the smooth running of the country's 69th National Day celebrations.

items.title: National Day: Early birds flock to Dataran Putrajaya for prime spots, best shots
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: Eager to witness the 69th National Day celebration up close, members of the public began gathering at Dataran Putrajaya as early as yesterday evening, with some camping overnight to secure prime viewing spots along the parade route. This time, we decided to come early to get a spot closer to the celebration and enjoy a better view," said Adib. Having arrived at about 5.30pm yesterday, Ahmad Azri said his family was thrilled to get a good viewing spot, giving the children a chance to experience the National Day celebration firsthand during the school holidays.

items.title: 'Proud and excited': RMAF chief leads National Day flypast [WATCH]
items.summary: The feeling, he said, was still one of pride and excitement, tempered by a comfortable sense of familiarity. More importantly, I see it as a responsibility to continue defending the country," he said. "Our readiness must be high.

items.title: Making a living in a shadow of history
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: At the ticketing entrance of Stadium Merdeka, Rusilawati Borhan, better known as Cik Comel, spent Ramadan selling kuih and nasi lemak as the historic landmark came alive again. MORE THAN A TRADING SPOT Cik Comel, 54, said setting up her stall at the stadium brought back memories of visiting the landmark with her husband when they were younger. "I opened my stall right at the stadium's ticketing entrance.

items.title: Restoring the home of Merdeka
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Stadium Merdeka, where Tunku Abdul Rahman proclaimed independence in 1957, is no longer a monument frozen in time. Even features that disappeared over the decades have been painstakingly recreated, bringing the stadium closer to is 1957 appearance, when Tunku Abdul Rahman Putra Al-Haj declared "Merdeka" seven times. For PNB Merdeka Ventures, the custodian of Stadium Merdeka, the challenge was to preserve its past without turning it into a relic.

items.title: Building Merdeka: How the nation‑building projects of 1957-65 shaped the early years of independence
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 31 — Before Malaya had even become independent, it was already building the place where independence would be declared. At Stadium Merdeka, Malaysia’s first Prime Minister Tunku Abdul Rahman proclaimed the independence of the Federation of Malaya. Over the next eight years, Kuala Lumpur acquired a national stadium, international-class hotels, Parliament House, a national museum, a national mosque, a national language institution, a major water-supply dam and a new international airport.

items.title: Cloud seeding planned for areas with high API readings
items.summary: CLOUD seeding will be carried out in areas where the Air Pollutant Index (API) reading exceeds 150, especially those at 200 and above. Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said the National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma), the Meteorological Department and the Royal Malaysian Air Force were already coordinating such operations in haze-hit areas. "Priority is given to areas where the API reading has reached 200," he said after launching Laman Usahawan Desa@Pameran Pertanian, Hortikultur dan Agropelancongan here yesterday.

items.title: Before Nepal floods, China was asked for early warnings as risks mounted
items.summary: At the May 27 meeting in Nepal's capital, 10 officials from Nepal and about a dozen from China, including the Tibet region where the disaster struck, discussed strengthening cooperation to monitor and respond to floods, weather and glacier-related hazards, according to an agenda prepared by the Nepali side and seen by Reuters. Nepali officials say the priority is to deepen cooperation with China. At the meeting, the Chinese said they did not have the mandate to sign an agreement to meet Nepal's requests, asking for further discussions, said Binod Parajuli, another Nepal government hydrologist.

items.title: Zambry: New committee to create framework for filling Auku vacuum
items.summary: AN independent committee will be established to study and recommend a framework for new legislation to replace the Universities and University Colleges Act 1971 (Auku). Higher Education Minister Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abd Kadir said yesterday repealing Auku required a transitional legal mechanism to avoid a legal vacuum, as it was the primary law governing public universities. Without an overarching legal framework, universities cannot operate.

items.title: Grand Canyon flash flood: More than 20 feared missing [WATCH]
items.summary: LOS ANGELES: More than 20 people may be missing after a flash flood in Grand Canyon National Park, the National Park Service said in a statement Sunday. The floods hit the Bright Angel Canyon and Phantom Ranch area on Saturday, the service said, adding that it was working with Arizona authorities to evacuate people and account for individuals in the affected area. The flash flood began about 2.30pm on Saturday.

items.title: Putin touts Russia's coal, mineral reserves
items.summary: MOSCOW: President Vladimir Putin said Russia holds the world's second-largest coal reserves and remains a global market leader despite the industry's current challenges, Russian News Agency TASS reported. "Our country has the world's second-largest coal reserves, ranks third in coal exports and sixth in production. Putin said the industry maintained coal production at 440 million tonnes last year.

items.title: US strikes Iran for first time in a month
items.summary: WASHINGTON: The United States said Sunday it had carried out strikes on Iranian rocket launchers on a small island in the Strait of Hormuz, its first attacks on Iran since late July. "Earlier today, US forces struck two Iranian launchers on Larak Island," a US Central Command spokesman said, adding that Iran's Revolutionary Guards "were observed preparing to launch rockets with sea mines into the Strait of Hormuz." "Last week, CENTCOM completed clearing sea mines from the strait's international shipping routes," said Navy Captain Tim Hawkins, a spokesman for US Central Command.

items.title: 'Venezuela owns its oil'
items.summary: INTERIM leader Delcy Rodriguez assured the public on Saturday that Venezuela retains control of its oil under a new agreement that allows the United States significant access to it. The US will have majority control of 65 billion barrels of Venezuela's proven reserves in what President Donald Trump described on Friday as "the biggest oil deal in world history". "One thing must be absolutely clear: Venezuela retains ownership and sovereignty over its resources," said Rodriguez in a speech on state television.

items.title: 69 years of Independence: Defining our vision for Malaysia
items.summary: LETTER: As we commemorate our 69th National Day on Aug 31, 2026, let us reflect on the meaning of Merdeka and the responsibilities that come with being a free and sovereign nation. Over the past 69 years, Malaysia has made significant progress. Economic pressures, geopolitical tensions, climate change, environmental challenges, technological disruption, serious corruption, social problems and concerns over safety and well-being are creating new challenges for our nation.

items.title: Norway's new King Haakon VIII, popular face of shaken monarchy
items.summary: AS comfortable in a duffel coat as in ceremonial dress, Norway's new monarch, King Haakon VIII, is the new face of a monarchy long praised for its modernity and modesty, but now beset by woe and scandal. Haakon automatically succeeded to the throne Friday after his father, King Harald, passed away peacefully earlier in the day. He has increasingly seen his family's affairs plastered across front pages: his wife's lung transplant, revelations about her ties to convicted US sex offender Jeffrey Epstein, a rape conviction against his stepson, and the escapades of his eccentric sister and her American self-proclaimed shaman husband.'

items.title: Police launch investigation into viral Wangsa Maju brawl involving group of men
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Police are investigating a brawl involving a group of men in the Wangsa Maju area that went viral on social media. City police chief Datuk Fadil Marsus said police had yet to receive a report regarding the incident. Earlier, a 38-second video went viral showing a car being driven at high speed before crashing into another car parked at the roadside.

items.title: Google Maps renames Lake Ontario 'Lake America' in US – but not Canada
items.summary: WASHINGTON: Google redesignated Lake Ontario as "Lake America" on maps seen by US users Sunday after President Donald Trump announced he was renaming the body of water, with a Canadian official slamming the cross-border tensions as "absolutely backwards." People in Canada will still see Lake Ontario, the Indigenous-rooted name used for the lake since the 17th century, on their devices and computers, the US-based tech giant said. "Since we update Google Maps to reflect name changes in official government sources, which is GNIS for the US, people using Maps in the US will see 'Lake America,' those in Canada will continue to see 'Lake Ontario,' and those outside of the US and Canada will see both names," Google said on its blog.

items.title: NASA launches Roman telescope on cosmic mapping mission
items.summary: Designed to take a panoramic view of the vast reaches of space, the Roman Space Telescope "will help unlock the secrets of the universe," US President Donald Trump said Friday during a ceremony at NASA headquarters in Houston, Texas. While Hubble revealed that the universe is expanding faster than previously thought, Roman will seek to answer some of the other unsolved mysteries, including those of dark matter and dark energy. "Roman will give the Earth a new atlas of the universe," NASA administrator Jared Isaacman said in April when he unveiled the project to the press.

items.title: Learn to belong to one another
items.summary: DEAR Malaysia, I have been trying to remember when I first understood what it meant to belong to you. So I grew up moving between languages without thinking much about which belonged to whom. And Malaysia, we have come a long way.

items.title: A childhood between nations
items.summary: Much less is written about the families who travelled with diplomats: spouses who rebuilt homes in unfamiliar cities, and children who moved between countries without quite understanding that the world unfolding around them would one day become history. I was one of those children. I was born in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia, into a Malaysian diplomatic household when Malaysia itself was still finding its place in the post-colonial world.

items.title: NST Leader: The chicken-and-egg crisis nobody's solving
items.summary: RISING chicken and egg prices, driven by closures of problematic poultry farms, are an upshot of the old chicken-and-egg paradox. Despite the incongruity, farms do meet domestic demand, but national supply is tight. Farms face a cause-and-effect dilemma: higher feed costs, especially from volatile global imports, and labour shortages raise production costs and stifle operations.

items.title: Patriotism, national assets and vibrant performances to take centre stage at Dataran Putrajaya tomorrow
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 30 — Ahead of tomorrow’s 69th National Day celebration, Dataran Putrajaya is fully prepared to stage a grand gathering of thousands of participants, a showcase of national assets, and vibrant performances designed to ignite the people’s patriotic spirit. Inspector General of Police Commissioner Datuk Seri Mohd Yusri Hassan Basri during the full rehearsal for the 69th National Day parade themed ‘Malaysia Madani: Kesejahteraan Dinikmati’ at Dataran Putrajaya August 29, 2026. The statehood component features, among others, a large Jalur Gemilang-bearing contingent accompanied by the army, navy, and air force cadet officers from the National Resilience Leadership Academy, National Defence University of Malaysia (UPNM), alongside a National Service Training Programme (PLKN) contingent.

items.title: Fashion designer Rizalman says adopted son stable, treated for liver injury after being dragged by lorry
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 30 — Fashion designer Datuk Rizalman Ibrahim says his adopted son, Umar Nail, is in stable condition but remains under close medical observation following internal injuries sustained in a road accident. Rizalman said, “Alhamdulillah, as of now, Umar is stable,” adding that his son “is still under close monitoring by the medical team, particularly for injuries to his internal organs, namely the liver.” Rizalman said he continues to pray for Umar’s strength and recovery as treatment progresses.

items.title: ‘We have one homeland, Malaysia’: Anwar urges Malaysians to keep the spirit of independence alive
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 30 — The spirit of independence must continue to be nurtured in the hearts and minds of every Malaysian, with all communities united to build the nation, defend their rights and uphold justice, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. Therefore, we must unite. “Who must unite?

items.title: AI for the People participants must complete six modules to receive free AI tools
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 30 — Participants in the AI for the People (AI Untuk Rakyat) programme must complete and pass six designated modules to qualify for a free three-month subscription to selected artificial intelligence (AI) applications and software. In a statement today, the Digital Ministry said the six modules are AI Nation 2030: The Madani Approach, CYBERSAFE for the People, Generative AI, AI Security, Agentic AI for All and Cloud for the People. Meanwhile, Digital Ministry secretary-general Datuk Fabian Bigar said the AI for the People programme was an important step towards ensuring youths not only understood AI technology but also had access to AI tools that could be used for learning, creativity and productivity.

items.title: Families of three missing Malaysians in Nepal hope for good news on their safety
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 30 — The families and friends of three Malaysian climbers reported missing following a flash flood and landslide in the Nepal-Tibet border area last Wednesday are still hoping for good news regarding their safety. The three climbers are Muhammad Muhaimin Azhad Noor Hadi, 27, Muhammad Adib Haikal Awang Mansor, 27, and Muhammad Zaki Othman, 29, who were reported uncontactable while undertaking a climbing activity in the Langtang Valley. Muhammad Muhaimin is from Gelugor, Penang, Muhammad Zaki from Kubang Semang, Bukit Mertajam, while Muhammad Adib Haikal is from Kulim, Kedah.

items.title: Fahmi: 15 govt hospitals among early recipients of RM1b allocation to boost digital access and electronic medical record rollout
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 30 — A total of 15 government hospitals are among the initial group that will benefit from an allocation of RM1 billion to strengthen the digital efficiency of the public health sector, said Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil. Fahmi, who is also the Madani Government spokesperson, said the allocation, which was increased from RM650 million as previously announced, would accelerate the implementation of the Electronic Medical Record (EMR) system as well as the provision of Internet access including public WiFi at health clinics and government hospitals. Meanwhile, Fahmi said the Ministry of Communications would help ensure that Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s message on various government assistance and successes was effectively conveyed to people.

items.title: Family of missing Malaysian in Nepal urges govt to bring all victims home
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 30 — After nearly five days of anxious waiting, the family of N. Kalaiselvi, 65, who remains uncontactable in Nepal, is urging the government to bring the missing Malaysians home, regardless of their condition. Her daughter, Kritikaa Joyce De Brito, said the family appreciated the Malaysian government’s efforts to coordinate the search and rescue mission, but acknowledged that their hopes were fading after nearly five days without contact. She said that even if rescue teams successfully reached the affected area, the chances of finding the missing Malaysians alive could be slim given the conditions there.

items.title: Anwar announces six immediate measures to ease cost‑of‑living pressures
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 30 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today announced six immediate measures for the people covering fuel subsidies, school maintenance, artificial intelligence (AI), healthcare digitalisation, e-Invoicing and microfinancing, which will take effect on September 1. He said all the measures were part of the government’s efforts to address the people’s concerns, particularly those related to the cost of living and pressures of daily life. Also present were Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil, Cabinet ministers and Chief Secretary to the Government Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar.

items.title: Public urged to plan journey, arrive early amid National Day road closures in Putrajaya
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 30 — Members of the public planning to attend the 2026 National Day celebration at Dataran Putrajaya, here, tomorrow, are advised to plan their journey and arrive early, following the closure of several major roads around the government administrative centre. The closures involve Seri Wawasan bridge, Seri Saujana bridge, Seri Gemilang bridge, Putra bridge and Seri Ehsan bridge, while Seri Bestari bridge and Seri Setia bridge will remain open. Several other routes are also expected to be affected, including Lebuh Bestari, Lebuh Setia, Lebuh Saujana, Lebuh Gemilang, Lebuh Wawasan, Lebuh Sentosa, Jalan Tun Hussein, Persiaran Barat and Persiaran Sultan Salahuddin Abdul Aziz Shah.

items.title: MB: Pahang strengthens mineral‑sector enforcement, orders probe after trailers suspected of moving minerals out of Raub site
items.summary: KUANTAN, Aug 30 — The Pahang government will step up enforcement against activities involving mineral resources to ensure that all such operations comply with the law. Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Wan Rosdy Wan Ismail said the state government would also not compromise with any party that disregards the stipulated licence, permit and approval requirements. He said intelligence efforts, including drone surveillance, detected three trailers suspected of transporting minerals out of the mining area before they were stopped for inspection by the Pahang Enforcement Unit (UPNP).

items.title: Ahead of National Day, Anwar urges Malaysians to protect the nation and stay united
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 30 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has urged the people to safeguard the country to the best of their ability and uphold unity as the pillar of Malaysia’s strength. He said independence meant being free to determine one’s own destiny and having confidence in the strength of a dignified people and a sovereign nation. he said.

items.title: Anwar: School maintenance allocation to rise from RM1b to RM1.5b in 2027
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 30 — The government will increase the maintenance allocation for all types of schools by 50 per cent, from RM1 billion to RM1.5 billion in 2027, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. He said the additional allocation will cover all priority school streams, including national schools, Chinese and Tamil national-type schools, religious schools, tahfiz institutions, pondok schools, and special education. Anwar said the Ministry of Education (MOE) will also mobilise efforts to visit every district starting next month to examine every application for school infrastructure repairs.

items.title: Ferry operators urge urgent dredging of Kuala Kedah, Kuala Perlis lanes, warn silted routes could disrupt Langkawi schedules during peak season
items.summary: ALOR SETAR, Aug 30 — Langkawi ferry operators are appealing to the federal government to expedite dredging works in the shipping lanes in Kuala Kedah and Kuala Perlis which are now experiencing silt deposits that affect shipping safety. Ferry Line Ventures Sdn Bhd operations manager, Lieutenant Commander (Retired) Norhafiz Abdul Wahid, said the increasingly shallow shipping lanes not only increase the risk to passenger ferry operations, but can also cause schedule disruptions and travel delays. “Based on previous operational records, passenger ferry services are capable of transporting up to 25,000 tourists a day during peak season,” he said in a statement today.

items.title: Anwar pledges billions in seized funds for health, education; eases rules for small businesses
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 30 — The government will channel billions of ringgit seized from illegal activities into public healthcare and education, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said today, leading a series of fiscal announcements he said were aimed at supporting low-income groups and small businesses. As part of broader relief measures, Anwar also announced a new RM200 million grant scheme under the Geran Sejahtera Madani programme to assist hawkers, small traders, night market vendors, and mothers working from home. The new threshold was among the list of measures Anwar said would provide "temporary relief" as his government aims to alleviate living cost pressure and help businesses.

items.title: Amirudin says Pakatan prepared for all scenarios, including solo Melaka fight if BN deal fails
items.summary: GOMBAK, Aug 30 — Pakatan Harapan (PH) is always prepared for any eventuality in the Melaka state election, including contesting on its own should negotiations on cooperation with Barisan Nasional (BN) fail to reach an agreement. PH election director Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari said, however, that sufficient room should be given to the party leadership to assess the best strategic options before any decision is finalised. He said the country’s political landscape remained dynamic and flexible, allowing each party room to determine its own approach in facing the election.

items.title: Sarawak Rivers Board warns Rajang journeys perilous as haze blinds boatmen, drought shrinks channels
items.summary: SIBU, Aug 30 — River transport users in Sarawak have been advised to plan their journeys carefully and exercise greater vigilance amid the current drought and haze conditions to avoid untoward incidents. Sarawak Rivers Board (LSS) chairman Dr Safiee Ahmad said the drought had caused river levels to fall, making navigation channels shallower and narrower, while haze had reduced visibility. He said river transport users could also obtain the latest information on river water levels and advisory services from regional LSS offices to help them plan safe journeys.

items.title: Debt dispute sparks armed George Town school fight, police arrest 13 suspects including minors
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Aug 30 — Police have arrested 13 male suspects, including three minors, to assist in investigations into a violent brawl involving weapons that occurred in front of Sekolah Jenis Kebangsaan Cina (SJKC) Kong Min branch in Air Itam here early yesterday. Penang police chief Datuk Dennis Lim said all the suspects, aged between 16 and 33, were arrested in five raids across the state through an operation conducted by the Criminal Investigation Department’s Vice, Gambling and Secret Societies Division (D7) of the Penang Police Headquarters, together with the Northeast District Police Headquarters Criminal Investigation Division and with assistance from the Central Police Station. Lim said police were also investigating a vehicle that allegedly struck one of the victims during the brawl, inflicting injuries.

items.title: Deputy minister presses Wisma Putra for hotline, briefings as 91 Malaysians missing in Nepal‑China
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 30 — Wisma Putra has been urged to establish a dedicated one-stop centre to provide direct, regular and consistent updates to the next of kin of 91 Malaysians who remain uncontactable following the disaster at the Nepal-China border. Deputy National Unity Minister R. Yuneswaran said the centre should be equipped with a 24-hour hotline, case reference numbers and officers who could be contacted at any time. He said coordination between Wisma Putra, the National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma), JBPM, Nepalese and Chinese authorities, travel agencies and telecommunications companies must be intensified to verify travel manifests, passport numbers, travel routes and the last known locations of the individuals.

items.title: Budi95 quota restored to 300 litres, Anwar announces goodies ahead of Merdeka celebration
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 30 — The monthly quota for petrol and diesel subsidies will be raised again, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim revealed today as he announced several goodies ahead of tomorrow’s Merdeka Day celebration. For diesel, the quota would be raised from 300 to 400 litres a month. Anwar said the programme would benefit 16 million people.

items.title: Melaka’s Ab Rauf to steer BN–Pakatan talks, Zahid says timing depends on dissolution
items.summary: SERDANG, Aug 30 — Barisan Nasional (BN) chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi says formal negotiations with Pakatan Harapan (PH) on possible cooperation for the Melaka state election will begin only after the state assembly is dissolved. “We are handing this to Datuk Seri Ab Rauf, and I believe he will hold formal discussions once the Melaka assembly is dissolved,” Zahid told BH. Separately, PH election director Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari said the coalition was waiting for Ab Rauf to indicate his readiness before negotiations could begin.
